note: sluice-request could print the phase list it just classified, and two sessions have now paid for its not doing so. scripts/sluice-phases.sh sluice_is_prose_only is directly callable and decides whether a candidate skips clients+heavy (~560s vs ~1690s), but nothing in the submit path echoes the verdict -- so a submitter states a phase expectation in the nudge and finds out from the run. I predicted prose-only for a range containing .claude/skills/closing-a-campaign/SKILL.md; .claude/ is not on the allowlist (docs/*, book/src/chronicle/*, book/src/frontier/*, book/src/open-questions.md, book/src/SUMMARY.md) and the classifier is all-or-nothing, so it took the full ladder. The Lefford queue session reports the same class of error two days earlier on campaign/the-lodestar, from classifying the delta since a stage gate when the classifier reads the MERGE PRODUCT against main -- which is the more interesting half: the mistake is not reading the allowlist wrong, it is classifying the wrong RANGE. An echoed verdict at submit time fixes both, costs one line, and needs no new logic because the function already exists and is already sourced there. Meanwhile the by-hand check is: source scripts/sluice-phases.sh, then sluice_is_prose_only with git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD.
